name: Giant's Causeway
notes_original: UNESCO basalt columns on the Antrim coast. Free to walk; visitor centre is National Trust.
description: Tens of thousands of interlocking basalt columns drop into the sea on the north Antrim coast. The stones are the draw; the official visitor building is optional.

name: Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge
notes_original: Rope bridge to a sea stack. National Trust; seasonal wind closures.
description: A short rope bridge links the mainland to a tiny basalt stack that salmon fishermen used for generations. Cross only when the National Trust has it open to weather.

name: Dunluce Castle
notes_original: Cliff-edge castle ruin between Portrush and Giant's Causeway.
description: A ruined castle sits on a basalt outcrop above the Atlantic, half a mile of cliff path from the Causeway coast road. The kitchens once fell into the sea; the walls that remain are still worth the ticket.

name: Navan Fort
notes_original: Emain Macha. Iron Age ceremonial enclosure west of Armagh.
description: A great earthen enclosure west of Armagh city, remembered as Emain Macha, the legendary capital of Ulster. The mound is quiet now; the visitor centre sits below the hill.

name: Walls of Derry
notes_original: Complete 17th-century city walls. Walk the circuit above the Bogside.
description: Derry's city walls are still a complete circuit, wide enough to walk as a rampart above shops and the Bogside murals. Cannon, gates and the Guildhall sit on the same hill.

name: Slieve Donard
notes_original: Highest peak in the Mournes and in Northern Ireland.
description: The highest of the Mourne Mountains rises straight from Newcastle strand. The granite cone is a hard walk in any weather; the view takes in both coasts on a clear day.

name: Marble Arch Caves
notes_original: Show cave in a UNESCO Global Geopark. Boat + walking tour.
description: A river cave under Cuilcagh mountain, shown as a boat-and-walk tour through limestone chambers. Tours stop when the Cladagh is in spate; book ahead in summer.

name: Beaghmore Stone Circles
notes_original: Bronze Age stone circles and cairns in the Sperrins.
description: Seven stone circles, cairns and stone rows sit in bog country in the Sperrins, uncovered when peat was cut. It is an open site: no ticket hut, just a lane and the stones.

name: Cliffs of Moher
notes_original: Atlantic sea cliffs. Visitor experience is paid; cliff path exists either side.
description: Eight kilometres of Atlantic cliff, with the official visitor building at O'Brien's Tower. The cliff path continues toward Doolin and Hag's Head if you want the edge without the exhibition.

name: Poulnabrone dolmen
notes_original: Portal tomb on the Burren limestone.
description: A portal tomb on the Burren pavement, a capstone on two uprights that has stood since the Neolithic. There is a small car park on the R480; the limestone underfoot is sharp.

name: Skellig Michael
notes_original: UNESCO monastery island. Boat landings weather-limited from Portmagee.
description: A pyramid of rock eight miles off the Kerry coast, with a sixth-century monastery on the summit. Landing is by small boat from Portmagee or Ballinskelligs and is often cancelled.

name: Carrauntoohil
notes_original: Ireland's highest mountain. Hydro Road / Devil's Ladder approaches.
description: Ireland's highest mountain sits in the Reeks above the Gap of Dunloe. The Devil's Ladder is the usual line and is steep loose stone; treat it as a proper mountain day.

name: Newgrange
notes_original: UNESCO passage tomb. Entry via Brú na Bóinne visitor centre.
description: A passage tomb older than the pyramids, aligned to the winter solstice sunrise. You reach it only on a shuttle from the Brú na Bóinne visitor centre across the Boyne.

name: Hill of Tara
notes_original: Royal ceremonial hill. Open earthworks; church and visitor room on site.
description: A low ridge of earthworks that was the ceremonial centre of early Irish kingship. The Lia Fáil standing stone and the mounds are free to walk; the old church holds a small exhibition.

name: Rock of Cashel
notes_original: Medieval cathedral and round tower on a limestone outcrop. OPW.
description: A cluster of medieval church buildings on a limestone crag above Cashel town — round tower, cathedral, Cormac's Chapel with its frescoes. The rock is visible from the N8.

name: Blarney Castle
notes_original: Keep and gardens. The stone is a queue; the grounds are the better half.
description: A medieval keep in woodland northwest of Cork city, famous for the stone in the battlements. The gardens and the poison garden are as much the visit as the kiss.

name: Mizen Head
notes_original: Signal station on Ireland's southwest tip. Bridge to the island.
description: The signal station on Ireland's south-west extremity, reached by a footbridge over a sea gorge. Weather and swell are the point; the museum is in the old lightkeepers' houses.

name: Dún Aonghasa
notes_original: Cliff-edge stone fort on Inis Mór. OPW. Boat from Rossaveel or Doolin.
description: A semicircular stone fort on the edge of a 90-metre cliff on Inis Mór. There is no barrier at the drop. Boats run from Rossaveel and, in season, from Doolin.

name: Kylemore Abbey
notes_original: Victorian castle-abbey and walled garden in Connemara.
description: A Victorian castle on a Connemara lake, later a Benedictine abbey, with a restored walled garden in the next valley. The N59 runs the shore below the façade.

name: Croagh Patrick
notes_original: Pilgrimage mountain over Clew Bay. Reek Sunday in July.
description: The cone above Clew Bay that pilgrims climb, many of them barefoot, on the last Sunday in July. The path from Murrisk is steep quartzite; the oratory is on the summit.

name: Slieve League
notes_original: Some of Ireland's highest sea cliffs. One Man's Pass is not a casual walk.
description: Sea cliffs that rise almost 600 metres from Donegal Bay. A road reaches a viewing point; One Man's Pass along the ridge is a serious walk in wind.

name: Errigal
notes_original: Quartzite cone, highest in Donegal. Short steep climb from the R251.
description: A pale quartzite cone, the highest mountain in Donegal, rising over Dunlewey and the Poisoned Glen. The path is short and steep on loose stone.

name: Glendalough
notes_original: Monastic city in a glacial valley. Round tower and two lakes.
description: A monastic settlement in a two-lake glacial valley — round tower, stone churches, and the Miners' Road around the upper lake. The visitor centre is at the valley mouth.

name: Kilkenny Castle
notes_original: OPW castle on the Nore, city-centre.
description: A restored castle on the River Nore in the middle of Kilkenny, with parkland behind it. The parade and the design centre sit across the street.

name: Clonmacnoise
notes_original: Early Christian monastery on the Shannon. High crosses and round tower.
description: An early monastery on a bend of the Shannon, with high crosses, a round tower and a graveyard of kings. The river is the reason it was here.

name: Rock of Dunamase
notes_original: Castle ruin on a rock east of Portlaoise. Open site.
description: A ruined castle on a limestone outcrop east of Portlaoise, looking over the Heath. There is no ticket office; a short path from the car park reaches the gatehouse.

name: Castletown House
notes_original: Palladian house. OPW. Parkland on the Liffey.
description: Ireland's first great Palladian house, set in parkland at Celbridge. The long axial avenue and the interiors are the visit; the café sits in the west wing.

name: Brownshill Dolmen
notes_original: Portal tomb with one of Europe's heaviest capstones.
description: A portal tomb in a field east of Carlow town whose capstone is among the heaviest in Europe. A short fenced path from the road; no staff on site.

name: Monasterboice
notes_original: Round tower and Muiredach's High Cross.
description: A round tower and two high crosses in a graveyard north of Drogheda. Muiredach's Cross is the reason to stop; the site is open and unstaffed.

name: Hill of Uisneach
notes_original: Ceremonial hill. Catstone. Guided access on the working farm.
description: A low hill in the midlands treated as the ceremonial centre of Ireland, with the Catstone erratic on its shoulder. Access is usually by guided walk on the farm.

name: Corlea Trackway
notes_original: Iron Age oak road preserved in a bog. OPW visitor building.
description: An Iron Age oak road, eight metres wide, preserved in a Longford bog and shown inside an OPW hall built over the timbers. The surrounding bog is still wet.

name: Rathcroghan
notes_original: Royal landscape of Cruachan. Visitor centre in Tulsk.
description: A landscape of earthworks around Tulsk that early sources treat as Cruachan, the royal site of Connacht. The visitor centre in the village orients you before the fields.

name: King John's Castle
notes_original: Angevin castle on the Shannon in Limerick city.
description: An Angevin castle on an island in the Shannon, with a modern exhibition inside the walls. King John's Bridge and the Treaty Stone sit on the same stretch of river.

name: Hook Lighthouse
notes_original: One of the oldest working lighthouses. Tours inside the tower.
description: A massive medieval lighthouse still in use on the Hook peninsula. Tours climb the tower; the headland around it is all wind and birds.

name: Glencar Waterfall
notes_original: Named waterfall in Glencar, on the Sligo–Leitrim border.
description: A named waterfall dropping into Glencar Lough on the Sligo–Leitrim border, a short walk from the car park. Yeats used the lake in print; the path is easy.

name: Benbulbin
notes_original: Flat-topped Dartry mountain. Walks from Gortarowey / Barnaribbon.
description: A flat-topped limestone mountain that defines the Sligo skyline. Walks start from Gortarowey forest; the plateau edge is a cornice in winter.

name: Dublin Castle
notes_original: State apartments and medieval tower in the city. OPW.
description: The castle that was the seat of British administration, now state apartments, a medieval tower and a garden on the site of the black pool that named the city.

name: Reginald's Tower
notes_original: Viking-era stone tower on the quays. Waterford Treasures.
description: A round stone tower on Waterford's quays, the oldest civic building in Ireland still in use, holding Viking and medieval finds from the city.

name: Cavan Burren Park
notes_original: Limestone upland with megaliths near the Fermanagh border.
description: A limestone upland on the Cavan–Fermanagh border, with megalithic tombs and a forest loop above Blacklion. The Cavan Burren is quieter than Clare's.

name: Clones Round Tower
notes_original: Round tower and high cross in Clones.
description: A truncated round tower and a high cross in the middle of Clones, remnants of an early monastery. The sarcophagus in the graveyard is carved in the shape of a house.

name: Howth Head
notes_original: Peninsula and cliff path east of Dublin. DART to Howth.
description: A peninsula east of Dublin with a cliff path, a lighthouse and views back to the city. The DART terminates at the harbour; the summit path starts above the village.

name: Phoenix Park
notes_original: Walled city park with deer, the Zoo, and Áras an Uachtaráin.
description: A walled park west of the centre, large enough for a herd of fallow deer, the Zoo, and the President's house. The Wellington Monument marks the main avenue.

name: Trim Castle
notes_original: Largest Anglo-Norman keep in Ireland. OPW.
description: The largest Anglo-Norman keep in Ireland, a square tower in a riverside ward at Trim. Guided tours go inside the keep; the walls can be walked without one.

name: Knowth
notes_original: Passage tomb with the largest collection of megalithic art. Shuttle from Brú na Bóinne.
description: A great passage tomb beside Newgrange, covered in megalithic carving. Like Newgrange it is reached only by shuttle from the Brú na Bóinne visitor centre.

name: Powerscourt Waterfall
notes_original: Ireland's highest waterfall, on the Powerscourt estate. Separate ticket from the house.
description: Ireland's highest waterfall, a separate ticket from the house and gardens at Enniskerry. A short valley walk; swimming is not the point and the rocks are slippy.

name: Great Sugar Loaf
notes_original: Quartzite cone inland of Bray. Short steep walk.
description: A quartzite cone inland of Bray, a short steep walk from a roadside car park. Dublin Bay and the Wicklow uplands both show from the summit.

name: Ross Castle
notes_original: Tower house on Lough Leane. OPW. Boat trips on the lake.
description: A tower house on Lough Leane, the starting point for boats to Innisfallen. The castle is OPW; the lake path is free.

name: Muckross House
notes_original: Victorian mansion in Killarney National Park. Gardens and abbey nearby.
description: A Victorian mansion in Killarney National Park, with gardens, a working farm and Muckross Abbey a short walk away. The house is ticketed; the park around it is not.

name: Torc Waterfall
notes_original: Waterfall in Killarney National Park, N71.
description: A cascade in oak woodland just off the N71 in Killarney National Park. The lower fall is a few minutes from the car park; the upper path continues toward Torc Mountain.

name: Gap of Dunloe
notes_original: Glacial breach through the Reeks. Jaunting cars from Kate Kearney's.
description: A glacial breach through the MacGillycuddy's Reeks, a narrow road between black lakes. Jaunting cars start at Kate Kearney's; cyclists and walkers use the same road.

name: Gallarus Oratory
notes_original: Boat-shaped dry-stone oratory on the Dingle Peninsula.
description: A dry-stone oratory shaped like an upturned boat, on the north side of the Dingle Peninsula. The visitor hut is optional; the oratory itself is the object.

name: Staigue Fort
notes_original: Stone ringfort in a Kerry valley. Small honesty box on the lane.
description: A thick-walled stone ringfort in a valley above Castlecove, with internal stairways in the wall. The last stretch is a farm lane; there is often an honesty box.

name: Charles Fort
notes_original: Star fort at the mouth of Kinsale harbour. OPW.
description: A star-shaped artillery fort at the mouth of Kinsale harbour, looking across to James Fort. The seaward ramparts are the walk; the exhibition is in the old barracks.

name: Garnish Island
notes_original: Ilnacullin. Garden island in Glengarriff harbour. OPW. Boat from the village.
description: A garden island in Glengarriff harbour, planted in the early twentieth century on a sheltered rock. A small ferry from the village is the only way on.

name: Gougane Barra
notes_original: Lake and oratory of St Finbarr. Forest park in a mountain corrie.
description: A lake in a mountain corrie where St Finbarr is said to have settled, with a small oratory on the shore. A forest park loops the cliffs above the water.

name: Aillwee Cave
notes_original: Show cave in the Burren. Birds of prey on the same site.
description: A show cave in the Burren above Ballyvaughan, with a short underground walk and a birds-of-prey arena on the same hillside. The café terrace looks north to Galway Bay.

name: Loop Head Lighthouse
notes_original: Lighthouse on Clare's western tip. Bridges of Ross nearby.
description: A lighthouse on the long finger of land that ends Clare. The Bridges of Ross and the cliff path are as much the visit as the light.

name: Fanad Head Lighthouse
notes_original: Lighthouse on Lough Swilly. Tours and keepers' cottages.
description: A lighthouse on the Atlantic side of Lough Swilly, with tours of the tower and keepers' cottages to stay in. The peninsula road is the long way round from Letterkenny.

name: Malin Head
notes_original: Ireland's most northerly point. Banba's Crown.
description: Ireland's most northerly point, a low headland of rock and a watch tower at Banba's Crown. The weather station and the WW2 lookout sit in the same wind.

name: Glenveagh Castle
notes_original: Castle and gardens in Glenveagh National Park. Shuttle from the visitor centre.
description: A nineteenth-century castle on Lough Veagh inside the national park, with Italianate gardens. A shuttle from the visitor centre is the usual approach; the park itself is open.

name: Céide Fields
notes_original: Neolithic field system under blanket bog. OPW pyramid visitor centre.
description: A Neolithic field system preserved under blanket bog on the north Mayo coast. The OPW building is a glass pyramid on the cliff; the fields are cut as sections in the peat.

name: Downpatrick Head
notes_original: Cliff headland and sea stack Dún Briste. Blow-hole.
description: A cliff headland on the north Mayo coast with a detached sea stack, Dún Briste, and a blow-hole in the grass. Stay back from the edge; the ground is undercut.

name: Diamond Hill
notes_original: Waymarked peak in Connemara National Park.
description: A waymarked quartzite hill in Connemara National Park above Letterfrack. The boardwalk path is the busiest walk in the Twelve Bens; the view is the Twelve Bens and the sea.

name: Cong Abbey
notes_original: Augustine abbey ruins in Cong village.
description: The ruins of an Augustinian abbey in Cong, with a later cloister and a dry canal nearby that never took water. The Quiet Man is filmed folklore; the stone is the visit.

name: Drombeg Stone Circle
notes_original: Recumbent stone circle in west Cork. Fulacht fiadh beside it.
description: A recumbent stone circle in west Cork, with a cooking pit beside it. The site is open from a small car park off the road between Glandore and Rosscarbery.

name: Jerpoint Abbey
notes_original: Cistercian abbey with carved cloister. OPW.
description: A Cistercian abbey south of Thomastown, known for the carved figures on the cloister. OPW staff the site in season; the ruin is beside the old Dublin–Waterford road.

name: Dunmore Cave
notes_original: Show cave with Viking-age finds. OPW.
description: A cave in limestone north of Kilkenny city, shown on a guided tour, with a Viking-age massacre in the record. The chambers are short; the steps are steep.

name: Tintern Abbey
notes_original: Cistercian abbey later a dwelling. OPW. Hook peninsula.
description: A Cistercian abbey on the Hook peninsula that became a family house, now an OPW ruin with a small exhibition. The estuary path is part of the visit.

name: Malahide Castle
notes_original: Castle and park in Malahide. Talbot Botanic Gardens.
description: A castle in a public park at Malahide, with Talbot botanic gardens beside it. The park is free; the house is a ticket. DART to Malahide.

name: Carrickfergus Castle
notes_original: Norman keep on Belfast Lough. State Care.
description: A Norman keep on a rock in Belfast Lough, still a complete enclosure. The harbour and the town sit against the walls.

name: Mussenden Temple
notes_original: Clifftop rotunda on the Downhill Demesne. National Trust.
description: A clifftop rotunda on the Downhill Demesne, a library built as a temple above the railway. The National Trust holds the demesne; the cliff path is the visit.

name: Grianán of Aileach
notes_original: Stone ringfort on Greenan Mountain. Views of Lough Swilly and Lough Foyle.
description: A restored stone ringfort on a hill above the Inishowen neck, looking at both Lough Swilly and Lough Foyle. A steep lane from Burt; the walls are high and windy.

name: Carrowmore Megalithic Cemetery
notes_original: One of Ireland's largest megalithic cemeteries. OPW. Knocknarea in view.
description: A spread of passage tombs on the Cúil Irra peninsula, with Knocknarea in view. The OPW visitor building sits among the circles; several tombs are in the surrounding fields.

name: Knocknarea
notes_original: Mountain cairn attributed to Queen Maeve. Walk from Strandhill.
description: A limestone hill west of Sligo with a huge cairn on top, traditionally Queen Maeve's. The path from Strandhill is a popular short climb; stay off the cairn itself.

name: Parke's Castle
notes_original: Plantation castle on Lough Gill. OPW.
description: A plantation castle on the shore of Lough Gill, restored as an OPW site. Boats on the lake and the road to Dromahair share the same shore.

name: Creevykeel Court Tomb
notes_original: Court tomb beside the N15. OPW.
description: A court tomb in a field beside the N15 at Cliffoney, one of the easier megaliths to reach from a main road. A short path from a lay-by.

name: Kilmacduagh
notes_original: Leaning round tower and cathedral ruins on the Burren edge.
description: A round tower that leans, and a cluster of church ruins, on the edge of the Burren near Gort. The site is open; the tower is among the tallest in Ireland.

name: Dunguaire Castle
notes_original: Tower house on Galway Bay at Kinvara.
description: A tower house on a spit in Galway Bay at Kinvara, a postcard of the Wild Atlantic Way. The medieval banquet is a separate product; the tower can be visited by day.

name: Aughnanure Castle
notes_original: O'Flaherty tower house. OPW. Near Oughterard.
description: An O'Flaherty tower house in woodland near Oughterard, with a double bawn and a river beside it. OPW in season.

name: Coole Park
notes_original: Lady Gregory's woods and turlough. Autograph Tree.
description: The woods and turlough that were Lady Gregory's Coole, with the Autograph Tree still standing. The house is gone; the park is a NPWS nature reserve.

name: Bunratty Castle
notes_original: Restored tower house and folk park beside the Shannon.
description: A restored tower house beside the Shannon, with a folk park of relocated buildings in the grounds. The castle is the artefact; the park is a museum of rural rooms.

name: Knappogue Castle
notes_original: McNamara tower house near Quin.
description: A McNamara tower house in east Clare, restored as a visitor castle near Quin Abbey. The banquet is evening-only; daytime visits cover the tower.

name: Quin Abbey
notes_original: Franciscan friary, well preserved. Village of Quin.
description: A Franciscan friary in the village of Quin, among the better-preserved in Ireland, with cloister and tower still standing. No ticket; watch your step on the stairs.

name: Athlone Castle
notes_original: Castle on the Shannon crossing. Visitor exhibition inside.
description: A castle on the Shannon crossing that still commands the bridge. The exhibition inside covers the siege and the river; the town is on both banks.

name: Fore Abbey
notes_original: Benedictine priory. Seven Wonders of Fore.
description: A Benedictine priory in a valley of the north Westmeath lakes, tied to the local 'seven wonders'. The ruins and the anchorite's cell are an open site.

name: Belvedere House
notes_original: House, gardens and Jealous Wall on Lough Ennell.
description: An eighteenth-century house on Lough Ennell with gardens and the Jealous Wall folly. The park is the walk; the house is a smaller interior.

name: Emo Court
notes_original: Gandon house and parkland. OPW.
description: A James Gandon house in parkland in Laois, with a long lake. OPW restored the interiors; the park is open more of the year than the rooms.

name: Portumna Castle
notes_original: Semi-fortified house. OPW. Forest park on Lough Derg.
description: A semi-fortified house at the head of Lough Derg, restored by OPW. Portumna Forest Park next door is the longer walk, with deer and lake shore.

name: Birr Castle Gardens
notes_original: Demesne, Leviathan telescope, and gardens. The castle itself is private.
description: A demesne in Birr with the Leviathan of Parsonstown — a historic telescope — and gardens. The castle remains a family house; the science and the trees are the public visit.

name: Cahir Castle
notes_original: Well-preserved castle on an island in the Suir. OPW.
description: A well-preserved castle on a rock in the River Suir in the middle of Cahir. OPW tours the interiors; the Swiss Cottage is a separate site upriver.

name: Swiss Cottage
notes_original: Ornamental cottage orné. OPW. Walk from Cahir Castle along the Suir.
description: A cottage orné on the Suir above Cahir, an ornamental cottage with a thatched roof and a theatrical interior. A riverside walk links it to the castle.

name: Ardmore Round Tower
notes_original: Round tower, cathedral and St Declan's stone. Cliff walk.
description: A round tower and ruined cathedral on the cliff above Ardmore, with Ogham stones and a cliff walk around the headland. St Declan's well sits on the path.

name: Kells Priory
notes_original: Augustinian priory with a walled precinct. King's River.
description: An Augustinian priory in a walled precinct beside the King's River at Kells, Co. Kilkenny. The enclosure is large and unstaffed; the village is not the Meath Kells.

name: Moone High Cross
notes_original: Tall granite high cross in a former monastery.
description: A tall, slender granite high cross in the ruins of a monastery at Moone. A glass roof now covers the cross; the site is a short pull-off from the N9.

name: Lough Gur
notes_original: Grange stone circle and visitor centre on a sacred lake.
description: A lake in east Limerick ringed with prehistoric sites, including the Grange stone circle. The visitor centre sits on the shore; several monuments are a short walk.

name: Kilmainham Gaol
notes_original: Historic prison. OPW. Book timed tickets.
description: The prison that held leaders of Irish rebellions, now an OPW museum on a timed ticket. Book ahead; walk-up is unreliable. The IMMA courtyard is next door.

name: Christ Church Cathedral
notes_original: Medieval cathedral and crypt in the Liberties.
description: Dublin's older cathedral, with a long crypt and a covered bridge over the street. The Liberties around it are the walking context.

name: Spike Island
notes_original: Fortified island in Cork Harbour. Ferry from Cobh.
description: A fortified island in Cork Harbour, a fortress and later a prison, reached by ferry from Cobh. Allow a half day; the island is walked, not driven.

name: Fastnet Lighthouse
notes_original: Rock lighthouse south of Cape Clear. View from the island or a boat; no public landing.
description: Ireland's most famous rock lighthouse, on a reef south of Cape Clear. There is no public landing; you see it from the island or from a boat out of Baltimore or Schull.

name: Connemara National Park
notes_original: NPWS park. Visitor centre at Letterfrack. Diamond Hill trail.
description: A national park of bog, mountain and Atlantic weather around Letterfrack. The visitor centre and Diamond Hill trail are the usual start; the Twelve Bens fill the skyline.

name: Killarney National Park
notes_original: Lakes, native oak and the Reeks. Muckross and Ross are inside the park.
description: Ireland's oldest national park: three lakes, native oak, and the edge of the Reeks. Muckross, Ross Castle and Torc are inside the boundary; Killarney town sits at the gate.

name: Burren National Park
notes_original: NPWS limestone pavement park. Trails from Mullaghmore / Gortlecka.
description: A national park of limestone pavement, turloughs and hazel scrub in the south-east Burren. Trails leave from Gortlecka and Mullaghmore; the visitor information is in Corofin.

name: Wicklow Mountains National Park
notes_original: Upland national park. Glendalough is the usual trailhead.
description: An upland national park of granite, bog and glacial valleys. Glendalough is the usual trailhead; the Military Road crosses the interior.

name: Glenveagh National Park
notes_original: Largest national park. Castle, gardens, and red deer.
description: Donegal's largest national park: a lake, a castle, and a herd of red deer in a glaciated valley. The visitor centre is the orientation; the rest is walking.

name: Cuilcagh Boardwalk
notes_original: Stairway to Heaven boardwalk onto Cuilcagh. Book parking in season.
description: A boardwalk onto Cuilcagh mountain, nicknamed the Stairway to Heaven. Parking is managed and often must be booked; the Marble Arch caves sit below the same hill.

name: The Gobbins
notes_original: Cliff path with bridges on Islandmagee. Guided, booked.
description: A cliff path of bridges and tunnels on Islandmagee, reopened as a guided walk. It is booked, not a casual stroll; weather and swell close it.

name: Titanic Belfast
notes_original: Museum on the slipways. Titanic Quarter.
description: A museum on the slipways where Titanic was built, in a building shaped like hulls. The dry dock and SS Nomadic sit on the same quay.

name: Mount Stewart
notes_original: National Trust house and world-class gardens on Strangford.
description: A National Trust house and garden on Strangford Lough, the gardens the equal of any in Ireland. The lough shore is part of the walk.

name: Slieve Gullion
notes_original: Ring-dyke mountain. Passage tomb on the summit. Forest drive.
description: A ring-dyke mountain south of Newry with a passage tomb on the summit and a forest drive around the lower slopes. The Ring of Gullion is the wider landscape.

name: Devenish Island
notes_original: Round tower monastery on Lough Erne. Ferry in season.
description: A monastic island in Lower Lough Erne with a round tower, reached by ferry from Trory in season. The tower is among the finest in Ulster.
